name: Lab Overlay Map
principle: Labs confirm phenotype. Genotype suggests what to check, not what to diagnose.

overlays.notes: MTHFR is not actionable without biomarkers.
Symptoms can mimic nutrient, sleep, or mood issues.
Use with waist/body-composition and lifestyle context.
Do not infer events from DNA.
Never change meds from raw DNA alone.

labs: CBC when bleeding is heavy or prolonged
ferritin when iron deficiency is possible
TSH when thyroid symptoms or cycle changes warrant it
reproductive hormone testing only when a clinician has a specific indication
overlays.notes: There is no single lab or DNA result that diagnoses PMS/PMDD. Prospective daily symptom timing across at least two cycles is more informative for the pattern; labs help evaluate mimics and consequences.

labs: MRI when ultrasound is insufficient or a specialist recommends it
overlays.notes: Adenomyosis is not diagnosed or excluded by consumer DNA. Symptoms, pelvic examination, and gynecologic imaging guide the workup; endometriosis, fibroids, pregnancy, and other causes may overlap.

labs: CBC and ferritin when bleeding is heavy, prolonged, or iron deficiency is possible
TSH/free T4 when symptoms, thyroid history, or changing bleeding warrant it
blood pressure, lipid panel, and HbA1c when cardiovascular or metabolic risk makes them clinically relevant
25(OH)D, calcium, PTH, and DXA only when bone, fracture, medication, or other clinical risk indicates
overlays.notes: Use age, bleeding or surgical history, symptoms, exact medication and supplement labels, and clinician evaluation. Do not use consumer DNA to stage menopause or order a routine hormone panel for every typical menopause question.

labs: CBC and ferritin when blood loss, fatigue, or iron deficiency is a concern
TSH/free T4 and thyroid antibodies when symptoms or thyroid history warrant it
glucose or HbA1c when gestational diabetes or metabolic risk is relevant
clinician-directed blood pressure, urine, or other testing based on postpartum symptoms and findings
overlays.notes: Postpartum timing, feeding, infant exposure, symptoms, and medications are user-supplied clinical context. DNA does not establish recovery or medication and supplement safety.
